QuestionStmt.S: Find standard enthalpy of formation of ammonia from following reaction. $$\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NH_3(g)}; \Delta_r H^\circ = -92.0 \, \text{kJ}$$

Solution.S:
Given reaction:

$$\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NH_3(g)}; \Delta_r H^\circ = -92.0 \, \text{kJ}$$

Step 1: Definition

The standard enthalpy of formation ($\Delta_f H^\circ$) is the enthalpy change when 1 mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states.

Step 2: According to the reaction

The above reaction forms 2 moles of ammonia (NH₃) and the enthalpy change is for 2 moles: −92.0 kJ.

Step 3: Find enthalpy for 1 mole

$$\Delta_f H^\circ = \frac{-92.0 \, \text{kJ}}{2} = -46.0 \, \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Step 4: Final Answer

So, the standard enthalpy of formation of ammonia is −46.0 kJ mol⁻¹.
